resources.string: What is true about DIA?
Duration of Insulin Action (DIA)
You should set the value for DIA in Insulin settings (Manage → Insulin settings), not in the profile.
The minimum allowed value is 5 hours.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/SettingUpAaps/ConfigBuilder.html#insulin
If you are satisfied that the value for DIA that you used in your pump before AAPS worked well, there is no need to change this when you start looping.
You should determine for yourself the appropriate value for DIA.
Hypo Temp-Target
What is the primary reason to set a hypo temp target?
To correct for hypos caused by incorrect basal rate settings.
To prevent AAPS from overcorrecting for a blood glucose rise caused by the fast-acting carbs used to treat a hypo.
To correct for a hypo induced as a result of exercise.
To prevent blood glucose from going low if there is already a 0% temporary basal rate running.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/TempTargets.html
Reasons for applying "Disconnect pump" in AAPS
This is unnecessary as insulin will not be delivered if the pump is physically disconnected.
It prevents AAPS from accounting for insulin that was not delivered whilst the pump is physically disconnected.
It will not stop insulin delivery if the pump remains connected to your body.
It will send AAPS into open loop mode.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/AapsScreens.html#loop-status
AAPS Settings
AAPS Settings
What are the best practices for backing up your settings?
You do not need to export your settings provided that you make a note of them.
Export your settings after you finish completing an objective.
Export your settings after changing any of your settings.
Export your settings after you finish your initial set-up and have set your Preferences.
Export your settings locally using the maintenance menu.
Your settings file is saved in the \"preferences\" folder inside the AAPS folder that you selected on your phone.
Copy your preferences file to a safe location outside of your phone (e.g. by using a cloud drive, connecting a cable to a computer, email, etc.)
If your phone is damaged or lost, there are easy ways to remotely recover your settings without a backup.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/Maintenance/ExportImportSettings.html
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/UsefulLinks/FAQ.html#what-emergency-equipment-is-recommended-to-take-with-me
Noisy CGM Readings
What should be done if CGM data is noisy?
Do nothing - AAPS will deal with it.
Disable the closed loop to avoid possible over or underdosing.
Replace consistently noisy or inaccurate sensors.
Make sure that your glucose data is smoothed, either by your CGM app or by a smoothing plugin in AAPS.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/CompatibleCgms/SmoothingBloodGlucoseData.html
Exercise and Profiles
How can you use profiles to best help the system deal with aerobic exercise?
Do a profile switch to less than 100%.
Do a profile switch to more than 100%.
Leave the profile set to 100%.
Suspend the loop.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/ProfileSwitch-ProfilePercentage.html
Exercise and Temporary Targets
How can you use temporary targets to best help the system deal with aerobic exercise?
Set an activity blood glucose target starting a suitable time before beginning exercise.
Set an activity blood glucose target after finishing exercise.
Leave your blood glucose target unchanged.
Wait until blood glucose drops below your hypo temp target and then eat 15 g of fast acting carbohydrates.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/TempTargets.html
Basal, ISF, and I:C Testing
When should these values be validated?
Before starting looping.
When experiencing frequent high or low blood glucose.
At least once per week.
Once set and validated, these values should not change over time.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/SettingUpAaps/YourAapsProfile.html
Prerequisites
What is essential to set up and use AAPS?
A way to build AAPS. Either via a browser or a computer with Android Studio installed.
A compatible insulin pump if you are planning to run a closed loop.
Nightscout or Tidepool, to keep a record of your data.
Experience in programming or editing code.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/Getting-Started/ComponentOverview.html
Prerequisites
What is essential to set up and use AAPS?
Validated values for your profile (basal rates, ISF, I:C ratio) and for your insulin (DIA).
A compatible Android device (e.g. mobile/cell phone, full Android watch, or tablet).
AAPS requires an internet connection to run in the closed loop.
A supported CGM and appropriate app to receive blood glucose values on the phone/device.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/Getting-Started/ComponentOverview.html
Updating AAPS
To build with Android Studio, you need Git installed and configured on your computer. Browser build does not need Git.
When updated versions of AAPS are released, the earlier versions may be remotely limited after a specified time.
If you build with Android Studio, you should save and note the location of your keystore and use the same signing key for updates as for your previous installation.
If you have difficulty building the apk, you can install an apk that has been built by a friend.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/Maintenance/UpdateToNewVersion.html
Troubleshooting
Where can you look for help with AAPS?
You can ask for advice in the AAPS Users Facebook group.
You should read (and re-read) the AAPS documentation.
You can ask for advice, discuss technical problems and feature requests in the AAPS Discord.
You can submit issues such as bugs and feature requests on GitHub.
You should ask your diabetes clinic/endocrinologist.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/GettingHelp/WhereCanIGetHelp.html
https://www.facebook.com/groups/AndroidAPSUsers/
https://discord.gg/4fQUWHZ4Mw
https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/issues
Insulin Settings
In Insulin settings, which of these insulins should use the ultra-rapid peak time of 55 minutes?
Fiasp®
NovoRapid®/Novolog®
Humalog®
Actrapid®/Humulin R®/"regular" human insulin.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/SettingUpAaps/ConfigBuilder.html#insulin
Sensitivity Plugins
Sensitivity plugins allow AAPS to adjust for temporary or short-lived changes in insulin sensitivity (for example hormonal changes or issues with absorption at the infusion site).
Sensitivity plugins provide the user with suggested changes to basal rates, I:C ratios, and ISF that can be used to edit profile.
Logging a cannula change will reset the Autosens ratio back to 100%.
Some of the plugin options have configurable time ranges and the user can set them.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/SensitivityDetectionAndCob.html
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/KeyAapsFeatures.html#autosens
Carb Entry Errors
What should you do if you’ve made an incorrect carb entry?
Delete the incorrect entry in Treatments history and enter the correct carb value.
Bolus with insulin using the Prime/Fill menu.
Do nothing – AAPS will make the appropriate adjustments.
Bolus with insulin using the Insulin button in the Treatments menu.
Insulin delivery/entry errors
What should you do if you received less insulin than the pump history suggests e.g. due to an occlusion, a failed cannula or forgetting to reattach the pump after a shower?
Delete insulin data from Nightscout Careportal to remove it from the pump history.
Compare values in AAPS and pump history (if pump supports this).
Bolus a proportion of your calculated ‘missed’ insulin by either syringe/pen or using a prime.
Carbs on Board (COB)
How does changing the ISF value affect the COB calculation in AAPS?
Increasing ISF will make the calculated carb absorption time longer.
Increasing ISF will make the calculated carb absorption time shorter.
Increasing ISF will not affect the calculated carb absorption.
How does changing the IC value affect the COB calculation?
Increasing IC will make the calculated carb absorption time longer.
Increasing IC will make the calculated carb absorption time shorter.
Increasing IC will not affect the calculated carb absorption.
How does changing the profile percentage affect the COB calculation?
Setting the profile to 150% will make the calculated carb absorption time longer.
Setting the profile to 150% will make the calculated carb absorption time shorter.
Setting the profile to 150% will not affect the calculated carb absorption.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/CobCalculation.html
IOB value is affected by issued temporary basals.
High temp basal will not be given when your blood sugar is below target.
Negative IOB for a substantial period in the absence of exercise suggests your profile is too strong and less insulin is needed in your settings.
Positive IOB for a substantial period suggests insulin resistance or unannounced meals.
Carb entry and boluses
Only grams should be used for estimating and recording carbohydrates consumed.
Carbohydrates consumed can be recorded using an appropriate exchange system (e.g. DAFNE "CHO" exchanges or European "Bread Units").
AAPS uses a dynamic model to estimate carb absorption and calculate COB.
If blood glucose levels are outside acceptable values (too low or too high) the bolus calculator can be used to provide suggestions for carb or insulin corrections.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/AapsScreens.html#bolus-wizard
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/SettingUpAaps/YourAapsProfile.html
e-carbs
What could you use e-carbs (extended carbs) for?
To schedule carbs in the future, possibly distributed over an interval (similar to an extended bolus distributing insulin over an interval).
For logging \'free\' exercise carbs you want to hide from AAPS.
e-carbs (distributed in the future) can assist AAPS in dealing with high fat/protein meals.
For logging rescue carbs you use to treat low blood glucose.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/ExtendedCarbs.html
Remote Monitoring and Control
How can you follow and control AAPS remotely (for example for your child)?
AAPSClient, the Nightscout app and the Nightscout web page all let you follow AAPS remotely.
Other apps (for example Dexcom Follow, or xDrip+ in follower mode) let you follow some data, such as glucose values, remotely. They may not show IOB or COB, or may calculate them differently.
To follow or control AAPS remotely, both phones need internet access (for example Wi-Fi or mobile data).
When AAPSClient is paired with the master phone, you can also control AAPS remotely, for example bolus, carbs, temporary targets, profile switch and loop mode.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/RemoteFeatures/RemoteMonitoring.html
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/RemoteFeatures/RemoteControl.html
Insulin Sensitivity Factor (ISF)
Raising ISF values will lead to more insulin delivery to cover a specific amount of carbs.
Reducing ISF values will lead to more insulin delivery to correct for an above target blood glucose.
Raising or lowering ISF does not affect insulin delivery when blood glucose levels are below target.
ISF should be entered in your AAPS Preferences.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/SettingUpAaps/YourAapsProfile.html
You can use more than one value for I:C ratio in your profile.
If you change your ISF in your profile you should always change your I:C ratio too.
Insulin to Carbohydrate Ratio (I:C ratio)
Higher I:C ratios lead to less insulin delivered for a given amount of carbs.
Lower I:C ratios lead to less insulin delivered for a given amount of carbs.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/SettingUpAaps/YourAapsProfile.html
Profile Switching
When specifying a 90% profile switch, which answers are true?
Basal rates will be 10% lower.
ISF will be 10% higher.
The value of the I:C ratio will be a 10% lower number.
ISF and I:C ratios will be unchanged.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/ProfileSwitch-ProfilePercentage.html
Profile Switching
When specifying a 120% profile switch, which answers are true?
Target blood glucose will be 20% higher.
Basal rates will be 20% higher.
Target blood glucose will be unchanged.
ISF will be 20% higher.
Profile Switching
If you get up 2 hours earlier than usual, how should you notify AAPS of the change in your schedule?
Initiate a profile switch with a timeshift of 2
Initiate a profile switch with a timeshift of -2
Set eating soon temporary target.
Do a profile switch to more than 100%.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/latest/DailyLifeWithAaps/ProfileSwitch-ProfilePercentage.html
Changes to profiles
Basal rates, ISF, I:C ratios, etc., should be set in profiles.
Activating changes to your Nightscout Profile requires your AAPS phone to have an internet connection.
Editing profiles to change values is sufficient to enact any changes made.
Multiple profiles can be set up and selected to accommodate changing circumstances (e.g., hormonal changes, shift working, weekdays/weekend lifestyle).
Other Medication. Please read the statement below and check the box to accept the declaration.

AAPS reduces basal rates or suspends insulin delivery to raise blood sugar. Drugs in the class SGLT2 inhibitors (gliflozins) can prevent increases in blood glucose and, thus, can produce a dangerous insulin deficiency leading to DKA. 
Common brand names are: Invokana®, Forxiga®, Jardiance®, Steglatro®, Suglat®, Apleway®, Deberza®, Synjardy®, Vokanamet®, Xigduo®.

I hereby promise that I will not take such drugs when using AAPS or will deactivate the loop before using such drugs.
Insulin Concentration Management
Before AAPS supported insulin concentrations, users ran U200 by setting a 50% profile to halve all values. In that setup, which answers are true?
My AAPS database and NS reports become wrong. All values (boluses, rates, TDD) must be multiplied by 2 to see the real values, especially for doctors and the health team.
I don\'t have to convert anything between AAPS and the pen if I use a U200 pen to give an external bolus.
Whatever pen I use to give an external bolus (U100 or U200), I have to convert between the amount calculated by AAPS and the amount I select on the pen, for every external bolus.
https://wiki.aaps.app/en/dev/AdvancedOptions/InsulinConcentration.html
You have been using the 50% profile workaround with U200 and want to switch to the Insulin Concentration feature. Which answers are true?
I can switch at any time, because I already have the correct U200 insulin in my pump.
I have to prepare a profile twice as aggressive (200% compared to current default profile) and synchronize this new profile after the next Patch/Reservoir change when the U200 insulin is selected.
I have to disable the DynISF feature for at least a week for the TDD to be perfectly consistent with the actual TDD value calculated in International Units.
After the switch, I will need to be very careful for several weeks, in order to get my brain used to thinking in international units regarding boluses, basal rates and TDD values.
You currently use U100 and plan to switch to another concentration with the Insulin Concentration feature. Which answers are true?
I have to modify my profile.
I should never use pump user interface (for tube pumps) to provide boluses.
I still need to manage conversion between AAPS and external boluses with Pen after the switch.
The Insulin Concentration can only be switched when the Insulin in the reservoir is changed or when a Patch/Pod is changed.
